value.title: Permitted access to research sources
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.
rules: Use a source's official API or download when it offers one, and read its terms first.
arXiv's APIs: no more than one request every three seconds, on a single connection, across every machine the requester runs; link to abstract pages instead of serving e-prints.
Crossref's REST API: use filters and select only the fields needed instead of one request per DOI, cache results, and back off on HTTP 429.
Retractions: check every cited DOI against Crossref's retraction data, through the update-type:retraction filter or the Retraction Watch data it publishes, before relying on it.
Web pages: read robots.txt and the site's terms, and stop when either forbids automated reading.
Facebook and Instagram content only through Meta's official research tools, such as the Meta Content Library and API, under their access terms, and never by scraping.
Paywalled full text only through access the requester already holds; never bypass a paywall or share the text.
No logins and no personal data, unless the requester grants a login explicitly for a source it licenses.

value.title: Screening sources, with a flow that adds up
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.
rules: Write the inclusion and exclusion criteria into the search plan before screening, and screen against them only.
Remove duplicates by DOI, then by normalized title and year, and count them.
Screen in two passes, title and summary, then full text, and give every exclusion one reason from the fixed list.
Exclude retracted works from the evidence and list them in the report.
The flow adds up: identified equals duplicates plus screened; screened equals excluded at title plus assessed; assessed equals excluded at full text plus included.

value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

levels.strong: Several independent primary sources agree and none credibly contradicts them.
levels.moderate: One good primary source, or several secondary sources that agree.
levels.limited: One secondary source, or primary sources that disagree.

rules: Grade claims, not sources alone, and say why in one line.
Self-reported, non-randomized or unmeasured results cannot make a claim strong by themselves.
A preprint, a press release or a news report cannot make a claim strong by itself.
The grade is a reading aid for the person who decides, not a certification.
